title: What carpenters do
d: Carpenters build the wooden skeleton and finish of buildings: framing, roofing, siding, stairs, trim, cabinets, and decks. Rough carpentry is structural; finish
description: Carpenters build the wooden skeleton and finish of buildings: framing, roofing, siding, stairs, trim, cabinets, and decks. Rough carpentry is structural; finish carpentry is the visible craft. It is one of the oldest trades and still learned largely by apprenticeship.

title: Essential tools
d: Tape measure, speed square, framing hammer, circular saw, miter saw, drill/driver set, levels (2 and 4 foot), chalk line, nail sets, utility knife, and a sharp
description: Tape measure, speed square, framing hammer, circular saw, miter saw, drill/driver set, levels (2 and 4 foot), chalk line, nail sets, utility knife, and a sharp pencil. Pros add: track saw, router, biscuit joiner, and a finish nailer.

title: Key skills
d: Reading plans, accurate measuring and layout, cutting to the line, framing walls plumb and square, hanging doors, installing trim with tight miters, and stair m
description: Reading plans, accurate measuring and layout, cutting to the line, framing walls plumb and square, hanging doors, installing trim with tight miters, and stair math. The 3-4-5 triangle squares everything; measure twice, cut once is the whole religion.

title: Safety essentials
d: Eye and ear protection with every power tool. Respect the blade: no freehand ripping, use push sticks, unplug for blade changes. Dust masks for sanding. Keep th
description: Eye and ear protection with every power tool. Respect the blade: no freehand ripping, use push sticks, unplug for blade changes. Dust masks for sanding. Keep the site clean — trips cause more injuries than saws.

title: Getting started
d: Start as a helper or laborer, learn framing first, then specialize. Formal apprenticeships run 3-4 years. Build a tool kit gradually — buy quality for what you
description: Start as a helper or laborer, learn framing first, then specialize. Formal apprenticeships run 3-4 years. Build a tool kit gradually — buy quality for what you use daily. Finish carpentry pays the premium.

title: Pro tips
d: Sharp blades cut cleaner and safer than dull ones. Glue plus fasteners beats fasteners alone. Caulk hides a multitude of sins in finish work — but tight joints
description: Sharp blades cut cleaner and safer than dull ones. Glue plus fasteners beats fasteners alone. Caulk hides a multitude of sins in finish work — but tight joints need none. Always check for square, level, and plumb before fastening.
